statement: A father and his son have ages that add up to 48 years. Six years ago, the father was 5 times as old as his son. How old is the father now?

choices.misconception: I found the son's age now and gave that.
I gave the father's age six years ago.
I took 6 years off the father's age but not off the son's.
I took 6 years off the son's age but not off the father's.

hints: Six years ago, both of them were 6 years younger.
Age problems: call the son's age now s, so the father is 48 - s. Write both ages six years ago, then turn the second sentence into an equation.
Six years ago they were s - 6 and 42 - s, so 42 - s = 5(s - 6).

solutions.reliable: Let the son be s years old now, so the father is 48 - s. Six years ago they were s - 6 and 42 - s, so 42 - s = 5(s - 6) = 5s - 30, which gives 6s = 72 and s = 12. The father is 48 - 12 = 36. Check: six years ago they were 30 and 6, and 30 is 5 times 6. The transferable idea: in age problems, move every person by the same number of years, then answer the question actually asked.
solutions.elegant: Six years ago their ages added to 48 - 12 = 36, and the father had 5 parts to the son's 1, so 6 parts made 36. The son was 6 and the father 30, so the father is 36 now.

whyOnTest: Age problems test moving both people back in time by the same amount, and the distractors are the other ages met on the way.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
